notes: SHIP v1.14.384 - HONEST NAMING + SCOPE FREEZE VERIFICATION. Owner froze the batch: no new features, finish the desktop shell, correct the defects, and prove no desktop styling leaks into the phone. This ship adds NO features. It makes three corrections and then runs the owner's seven-step verification end to end. CORRECTION 1 - THE PANEL NAME WAS DISHONEST. 'Site Health' implied facility, power-domain, cooling and network-fabric telemetry that PHANTOM does not receive and has no path to receive. Renamed to LOCAL SYSTEM STATE and captioned, in the panel itself, 'Read from this device. PHANTOM receives no facility telemetry.' Its rows are now only what the app genuinely knows from local state: connection, local store, site profile, Master file, active deployment, open blockers. No power, cooling, fabric or infrastructure row exists anywhere in the shell. CORRECTION 2 - READINESS IS NOW TRANSPARENT AND CLEARLY LOCAL. The score is still four real gates - site profile confirmed, Master loaded, zero open blockers, handoff started - and the mock's fixed 82% is still not reproduced. The summary now reads as a COUNT, 'N of 4 ready', because phrasing it as a count is what makes it legible as a local calculation rather than a monitoring readout, and the panel is captioned 'Calculated on this device from the four gates below.' Every gate is listed with its own OK or OPEN state, so the number can always be checked against its inputs. Nothing on this dashboard is framed as AI telemetry or external monitoring. CORRECTION 3 - THE FLAG NOW ACCEPTS BOTH SPELLINGS. The owner's verification order calls it ?shell=1; the ship called it ?cshell=1. cshell_isOn() now accepts either. A flag that silently does nothing on the URL someone actually types is a guaranteed field failure, not a naming quibble. Still non-persistent either way - it reads location.search and never writes storage. HARDENING: the .cs-dpanel hide rule was unscoped. It had been scoped to body.rd.cshell, which meant the desktop-only panels relied on #cmd-shell being display:none to stay hidden on the bare URL. That worked, but by inheritance rather than on their own terms, and correct-by-accident is not correct. SEVEN-STEP VERIFICATION, ALL PASSED, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED.
